newsitem.title: JAMAICA: CRICKET-RAIN FOILS W.INDIES AS FIRST TEST ENDS IN DRAW.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-RAIN FOILS W.INDIES AS FIRST TEST ENDS IN DRAW.

text.p: Rain deprived the West Indies of an outside chance of victory as the first test against India petered out into a draw on Monday.
The West Indies, inspired by a lightening 78 by Brian Lara, had piled on the runs in their second innings during Sunday's last session to give them an overall lead of 322 and a sniff of victory.
But their hopes of bowling out the Indians on the final day were foiled when rain prevented any play before tea.
When the game got under way, West Indies captain Courtney Walsh immediately declared at 241 for four.
However, India comfortably survived the last final session, scoring 99 runs for a loss of two wickets before the umpires abandoned play for good because of bad light.

West Indies debutant paceman Franklyn Rose was named man-of- the-match, claiming the scalp of opener Vangipurappu Laxman to add to the six wickets he had taken in the first innings, when he finished with 6-100.
Rose, 25, only returned to regional cricket with Jamaica this season after a self-imposed break.

Rahul Dravid got valuable batting practice with an unbeaten 51, in which he faced 130 balls and hit five fours, while captain Sachin Tendulkar reached double figures for the first time on tour as he progressed to 15 not out.

India had lost Navjot Sidhu for nought in the fourth over, caught by Holder at short leg off Walsh. Sidhu, on his first overseas tour since walking out on the squad in England last year, had also performanced disappointingly in the first innings when he made only ten.
Laxman (27) and Dravid then shared in a second wicket partnership of 62 before Laxman, driving extravagantly, was caught by Holder off Rose.

West Indies fast bowler Ian Bishop left the field early in the Indian innings because of what was described as a tightened hamstring and may be doubtful for the second test which begins in Port-of-Spain, Trinidad, on Friday.
